rationale: The question is how well a fast bedside test agrees with the reference standard for triage, which is a diagnostic accuracy question. Validating pre-specified cut-offs in consecutive patients, with blinded testers and a rule for patients who cannot complete the reference test, addresses the biases of the published studies (c2, c3). Reporting follows STARD.
alternatives: Randomised comparison of bedside and exercise-test triage (deferred: needs evidence of adequate accuracy first)
Derive a new prediction model from many variables (refused: overfitting with about 180 patients)
Switch triage now (refused: published cut-offs were never validated)
whyNotMoreComplex: A randomised comparison of triage strategies would be the next step only if a bedside test proves accurate enough.

decision.statement: Pursue a validation study of the 30-second sit-to-stand test (cut-off 10 or fewer, pre-specified from c1) and four-metre gait speed against exercise testing in about 180 consecutive patients, with blinded testers, cut-offs validated rather than derived (c2), patients unable to complete exercise testing classified by a pre-specified rule (c3) and a sample size based on sensitivity precision (c4).
decision.question: Should the prehabilitation team validate bedside tests against exercise testing before using them for triage?

criteria.text: A bedside cut-off with promising but unvalidated accuracy exists, and waiting for exercise testing delays prehabilitation.
No bedside cut-off reaches a sensitivity of 75 percent acceptable to the triage group.

gates.requirement: Physiotherapy department agreement to run the bedside tests at pre-assessment
gates.evidence: Memo PT-26-07 dated 2026-08-30, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: REB approval of the accuracy study with consent for exercise testing within two weeks

alternatives: Switch triage to the sit-to-stand test now on published accuracy
Buy exercise testing capacity instead of validating bedside tests
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c4; the unrated gait speed abstract (c5) supplies only a candidate cut-off and is not relied on. The physiotherapy gate is met; the REB gate stays unknown until the committee meets.

summary: Diagnostic validation study recommended; physiotherapy gate met, REB gate unknown.
